Subject: Registration webhook field mapping + DocuSign speaker release for BrightCloud sponsor

Carlos / Team —

Quick sync on the BrightCloud webinar next month. We need to finalize two items before I sign off on the sponsor insert and release flow:

1) Registration webhook mapping into HubSpot (and the one-pass that ON24 will call). We need a single CSV that maps ON24 field names -> HubSpot properties -> Redwood event IDs. Please include the following fields at minimum: first_name, last_name, email, company, job_title, country (ISO2), marketing_opt_in (boolean), sponsor_interest (multiple).

2) Speaker release: sponsor requires a signed speaker release for the pre-recorded segment. Laura is going to provide our standard DocuSign template but I need to confirm two things: whether ON24 can pass registrant email + registrant_id to DocuSign so we can pre-fill signer info and whether we can attach the signed artifact to the HubSpot contact record automatically.

Deliverables & timeline:
- ON24: mapping CSV + confirmation on webhook payload shape by Tue 2027-04-27 EOD
- Redwood events (Laura/Tessa): DocuSign template + HubSpot attachment flow details by Wed 2027-04-28 noon PT
- All: schedule a streaming dry-run (ON24 staging + Zoom fallback) for Fri 2027-04-30 morning PT

Attachments: I’ll upload a mapping CSV stub and our runbook link after this sends — marking placeholders below.

Thanks,
Markus

Hi Markus —

Thanks for the clear list. I attached a first-pass mapping file (webinar_webhook_mapping_v1.csv). Notes below:

- Payload shape: ON24 webhook sends a JSON body with field keys that match the left column in the CSV. We can include registrant_id and registrant_email for any event if requested.
- Pre-fill to DocuSign: we support sending a pre-fill payload to DocuSign via our integration hooks, but it’s a two-step flow — ON24 -> Redwood backend -> DocuSign. We will need the DocuSign envelope template ID and the parameter names to match.
- Attachment to HubSpot: ON24 can POST the completed envelope PDF to an endpoint you provide. HubSpot accepts files via the attachments API; we can push to a Redwood-managed endpoint that then writes to HubSpot.

Operational constraints and recommendations:
- Use "registrant_id" as the unique primary key in the mapping — it’s stable across exports and tracing.
- For GDPR regions, we only send email hashed if requested — confirm your retention policy.
- Staging endpoints: staging.on24.com/webhook/stage (recommended) and staging.on24.com/stream/edge-{region} for STAGE stream tests.

I’ve cc’d Tessa to make sure the runbook covers the envelope handoff and signing callback. If that looks good we’ll lock the CSV and schedule the staging test.

Best,
Carlos Vega
Integrations Engineer, ON24
cvega@on24.com

Markus / Carlos —

Attaching our current speaker_release_template_v3.pdf (redwood standard). A few clarifications from legal and ops:

- The template expects signer_name, signer_email, and signer_affiliation pre-filled. If ON24 can push those fields into the DocuSign template we can shorten the signing flow to one click for speakers.
- We need the signed artifact stored against both the HubSpot contact and the BrightCloud sponsorship record. HubSpot property for file: "files_speaker_release" — please confirm ON24 can POST to a Redwood endpoint with the envelope PDF and metadata: {registrant_id, event_id, sponsor_id}.
- Retention: Legal requires we keep signed releases for 5 years; please confirm retention on the staging test and whether the ON24 staging envelope will persist after testing.

Also — BrightCloud requested that a sponsor pixel be fired on the registration confirmation page (for attribution). We need to ensure the pixel does not transmit full PII (only hashed id and non-identifiable campaign info). Emily (BrightCloud) is on this thread to confirm the pixel payload.

Laura Bennett
